items.title: Clarifications sur la cession du gisement pétrolier El Menzah à Exxoil
items.description: Khaled Bettine, PDG de la Société nationale de la distribution des pétroles (SNDP-Agil), a apporté, dans une publication sur son compte Facebook , des précisions concernant les informations circulant au sujet de la cession, par l’État, du gisement pétrolier d’El Menzah dans le golfe de Hammamet. Il s’agit, en réalité, de la régularisation d’une situation juridique et administrative en suspens depuis 2001, a-t-il indiqué, en précisant que ce gisement a été découvert en 1998 et est entré en phase de production en 2000. L’exploitation a cessé en 2007, suite à une baisse de la production tombée à environ 35 barils par jour ; la production totale cumulée, sur toute la période d’exploitation, s’est élevée à près de 1,9 million de barils, a-t-il ajouté, en soulignant que l’Entreprise tunisienne d’activités pétrolières (Etap) avait décidé, en 2001, de ne pas participer au développement et à la production du gisement. Toutefois, la décision d’octroi de la concession d’exploitation, émise en novembre 2000, n’a pas été mise à jour en temps opportun, ce qui a maintenu la situation juridique dans un état nécessitant une régularisation. En 2024, la société Exxoil a déposé une demande de modification de la décision d’octroi de la concession, suite à la faillite de la société Ecumed Petroleum Grombalia en 2021. Selon les informations relatives au dossier, le Comité consultatif des hydrocarbures, l’instance publique chargée de donner des avis obligatoires et conformes ou consultatifs au ministre de l’Energie sur les questions relatives aux titres miniers (permis de recherche, concessions d’exploitation), a approuvé, en septembre 2024, le transfert des droits et obligations de la société en faillite à Exxoil (Groupe Setcar). Bettine a par ailleurs souligné que l’entreprise en question envisage de mener de nouvelles opérations d’exploration, des estimations suggérant que le gisement pourrait receler des ressources pétrolières encore non découvertes. Rappelons que la cession de la concession d’exploitation du gisement d’El Menzah à la société Exxoil a suscité une vive controverse. Le député Imed Ouled Jibril a notamment exigé des clarifications officielles concernant la nature des droits cédés, leur valeur financière, ainsi que la contrepartie — le cas échéant — perçue par l’Etap. Il a également interrogé les autorités sur les revenus attendus pour l’État, ainsi que sur les engagements de la société en matière d’investissements et de protection de l’environnement. Par ailleurs, le député a appelé à la publication des accords, des études d’évaluation et des documents afférents à cette décision, et a réclamé que l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) puisse y avoir accès afin d’exercer sa mission de contrôle, en insistant, en outre, sur la nécessité de garantir la transparence, de préserver les droits de l’État et de défendre l’intérêt national. Les clarifications de M. Bettine sont certes les bienvenues, mais la polémique à ce sujet aurait pu être évitée si l’État avait fait preuve de davantage de transparence et de moins de cachotteries d’un autre âge. S’agissant de ressources nationales, les Tunisiens sont en droit de tout savoir sur les tenants et les aboutissants de toute opération à caractère économique et commercial engageant la responsabilité de l’État. I. B. L’article Clarifications sur la cession du gisement pétrolier El Menzah à Exxoil est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Ensign Global, University of Utah graduate 20 entrepreneurs under business creation programme
items.description: Ensign Global University and the University of Utah have graduated 20 entrepreneurs from the second cohort of the Master of Business Creation (MBC) programme, an initiative designed to help business owners strengthen their enterprises and create employment opportunities. The programme takes a practical approach to entrepreneurship education, allowing participants to apply lessons in areas such as marketing, financial projections and human resource management directly to their businesses. President of Ensign Global University, Professor Stephen Alder, said the initiative could help address Africa’s employment challenges by equipping graduates to create jobs rather than rely solely on existing vacancies. Speaking at the graduation ceremony, Professor Alder said the continent produces millions of higher education graduates each year, while the number of available jobs remains limited. “If you look at the African continent, for example, there are about 12 million graduates from higher education every year. Yet it’s estimated that there are reasonably three million jobs for those 12 million graduates, meaning that three quarters of the graduates are not going to find successful employment,” he said. He said the business creation approach was intended to help participants build their own economic opportunities instead of depending entirely on the labour market. “This business creation approach is now designed to say, we’re not sort of creating graduates and then send them out to hope they find a job. But instead, they are creating their own future,” Professor Alder added. Programme focuses on existing businesses The MBC programme is delivered through a partnership between Ensign Global University and the University of Utah, based in Salt Lake City in the United States. Global Director of the programme, Jeff Davis, said it differs from conventional graduate programmes because admission places greater emphasis on business ownership than on academic qualifications alone. “We call it an MBA for entrepreneurs. So the most important criteria is not so much that you have an undergraduate degree but that you actually have a company. So you come in with a company to have a highly applied curriculum,” he said. Mr Davis explained that participants complete assignments based on their own businesses rather than relying on conventional examinations and theoretical case studies. “Every assignment, there are no quizzes, no tests, no textbooks, no Harvard case studies. Everything is an assignment on your company. Marketing plans, financial projections, HR organization,” he said. The approach is intended to help entrepreneurs apply what they learn to practical business challenges while developing strategies for growth. Building an entrepreneurial community Mr Davis said the programme also seeks to establish a community of entrepreneurs who can support one another beyond the classroom. “I think one of the most important things we’re building is not so much a program in Africa but we’re building a movement, a community of builders and dreamers and doers,” he said. On post-graduation support, he pointed to opportunities available through the University of Utah’s Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute, which supports entrepreneurs and business development. He said the institutions were also exploring possible funding opportunities for businesses in Africa. “At the University of Utah we have a very nationally ranked Institute called the Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute and we have programs for graduates from the MBC and people beyond the curriculum there in the United States. And so we’re also exploring funding for the companies here in Africa as we continue to build our entrepreneurs here in Africa,” he said. Applying classroom lessons to business Facilitating Lecturer Nana Dr Oboafo Kwamena Asumang Appiah I said the programme enables entrepreneurs to translate classroom learning into practical improvements within their businesses. “It’s Masters of Business Creation. It’s experiential, meaning that whatever you learn in school, you apply it directly to your business,” he said. He explained that participants are expected to implement lessons immediately, particularly in areas such as financial management and business development. “So if you talk about finances, you go and apply the financial models that we taught you in the classroom to your business, and then you take action,” he added. The graduation of the second cohort marks another stage in the partnership’s efforts to support entrepreneurs as they develop their businesses and pursue growth. The programme is expected to help participating founders strengthen their operations, expand their enterprises and create employment opportunities, while building connections with other entrepreneurs.

items.description: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday raised the key policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 per cent, its first increase since April as inflation, fuelled by high energy costs due to the Gulf conflict, remained above target. In a statement, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) said it had decided to increase the policy rate, with a majority decision of nine out of ten members. It noted that the “intensification in the Middle East conflict and low prospects of its near-term resolution” were keeping global energy prices at persistently elevated levels. “While the impact of this global shock on the domestic economy has remained contained so far amidst proactive monetary policy adjustment and continued fiscal discipline, geopolitical developments have worsened the inflation outlook as compared to the earlier assessment,” it said. It went on to say that although the external account and growth outlook remained broadly unchanged, risks had also increased. “Considering these developments and the evolving risks, the MPC deemed today’s decision as necessary to keep inflation expectations anchored, contain second-round effects of the ongoing supply shock and bring inflation within the target range of 5-7pc. This will help preserve macroeconomic stability, which is necessary for sustainable economic growth,” it said. It said that forex reserves had remained stable at around $21bn, Pakistan had reached a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and that real gross domestic product (GDP) growth had been revised at 3.7pc, almost unchanged from the initial estimate. It further said that the Federal Board of Revenue had exceeded its revenue collection target during the first quarter of the current fiscal year, major central banks had raised interest rates in the wake of rising inflationary pressures and the IMF had also revised its global inflation projections upwards. “While noting these developments and the increasing frequency of global supply shocks, the MPC emphasized the importance of increasing external and fiscal buffers to further strengthen the economy’s resilience. The committee also reiterated that continuing the prudent monetary and fiscal policy mix, alongside timely implementation of structural reforms, is essential for achieving higher and sustainable economic growth,” the statement said. Regarding inflation, which eased to 10.3pc in September from 11pc in Augus, the MPC said that the re-escalation in the Middle East conflict and domestic wheat supply frictions were two major factors keeping inflation at elevated levels It said that their expected continuation over the next few months had “worsened the inflation outlook”. It added that there was a risk that elevated food and energy inflation may further increase inflation expectations, which may seep into core inflation going forward. “In view of these developments and increasing risks to the inflation outlook, the committee assessed today’s decision as important to keep the real policy rate adequately positive on forward-looking basis. This is necessary to bring inflation within the target range over the medium term. The inflation outlook is subject to multiple risks, including geopolitical tensions, global commodity price volatility, unanticipated adjustments in energy tariffs, further uptick in wheat and allied product prices and adverse weather conditions,” it said. Regarding the external sector, the statement said that exports were recovering, adding that remittances had remained resilient and were projected to turn out higher than the earlier assessment. It said that the current account deficit in FY27 was assessed to remain within the earlier projected range of 0-1pc of GDP. “This, along with higher financial inflows, is expected to increase SBP’s FX reserves beyond the current level. This outlook, however, remains susceptible to multiple risks, including elevated global commodity prices, tightening international financial conditions, and supply constraints,” it said. As per the statement, the committee expected GDP growth to remain within previously projected ranges of 3.5pc to 4.5pc in FY27. However, it added that the outlook was susceptible to risks from escalation in the Middle East conflict and adverse climate events such as El Niño conditions. SBP governor cites inflationary outlook SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed also addressed a press conference to announce the decision and said there were many “underlying factors” behind the decision, especially the inflation outlook. He cited the US-Israel war on Iran and its impact on energy and oil prices, developments in the domestic market and the subsequent impact on inflation. He said that nine out of ten MPC members voted to raise the policy rate, while one member had a different view; they were of the opinion that it should be raised further. He said that consumer expectations and other forecasters’ views were taken into consideration, as well as other macro factors, especially the impact of global commodity and oil prices on the external account and the impact of remittances and export trends. Ahmed noted a deterioration in the current account since the last MPC meeting. However, he added: “The good thing is that its impact is still between zero and one per cent of GDP and it will stay between that.” He also shared that the central bank revised its outlook on remittances, from $44 billion to $45bn. On exports, the SBP governor said the trend was witnessing an improvement; however, it was not yet in line with the economy’s needs. He added that the bank estimated imports to be close to $71bn. He said it would take longer than planned for inflation to get within the target range and revised GDP growth to 3.7pc for the current fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. Meanwhile, Topline Securities said the central bank had raised the policy rate “in line with our expectations”. Previously, the policy rate was 11.5pc. The central bank had held the rate steady since raising it by 100 basis points in April in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks — its first increase in nearly three years. The SBP has cut the key rate by a cumulative 1,050 basis points since mid-2024 , from a record 22pc reached in June 2023, as inflation cooled sharply from multi-decade highs. Last week, the IMF called for Pakistan’s fiscal policy to go beyond achieving primary balance targets and protecting debt sustainability by reinforcing policy credibility, fostering economic recovery and creating space for public investment and social spending to support stronger long-term growth. Additional input from Reuters

items.title: EchoHouse founders Beryl and Bright Agyekum-Ayaaba graduate as joint valedictorians
items.description: Nearly two decades after turning a university magazine into EchoHouse, a marketing agency operating in eight countries, married founders Beryl Agyekum-Ayaaba and Bright Mamud-Ayaaba have reached another milestone in their journey together, graduating as joint valedictorians from a Master of Business Creation programme. Together since 2006 and married for 10 years, the couple has built their business and personal lives in tandem, learning to balance marriage, parenthood, entrepreneurship and academic demands while growing EchoHouse from a campus idea into an international company. For Bright, sharing the honour with his wife was both surreal and deeply personal. “The experience of being called on stage as a valedictorian together with my wife was quite surreal,” he said. “It’s not been an easy experience through the academics and working together as well, but we’ve kept pushing on. It’s been a whole year of rigorous assignments and meetings and all that, but we managed to combine that with work. It hasn’t been easy, but we are very proud of ourselves today.” The achievement followed a demanding year in which the couple combined academic work with the responsibilities of running a growing business. It also reflected a partnership built around shared ambition, resilience and an understanding of each other’s strengths. Even as they shared the spotlight, Bright was quick to credit his wife. “For me, I’ve always said it should be Beryl. She pushes me more, so she basically deserves it. I’m the guy in the back, you know, so I was very happy when we both got it, but I’ll give it to her. It’s hers,” he said. His remarks offered a glimpse into a relationship in which success is celebrated collectively rather than claimed individually. The couple’s entrepreneurial journey began while they were university students. In 2008, they started what would become EchoHouse as a magazine intended to tell the university’s story. The initiative eventually evolved into a full-service marketing agency, taking the founders into an industry far removed from their academic training. Both studied civil engineering for their first degrees but went on to build a business in marketing and related services. “We have a background of civil engineering, and that’s what we did for our first degree, and our business is in a totally different world, marketing services and all that,” Bright said. Their transition into the industry required them to develop new skills, learn through experience and navigate the uncertainties of entrepreneurship. They also had to build a viable business model and confront the challenge of securing the resources needed to support growth. Today, EchoHouse operates in eight countries, marking a significant evolution from its beginnings as a university publication. The company’s growth has demanded more than an initial idea. It has required the founders to develop their leadership, understand the practical demands of expansion and establish a working relationship that allows both to contribute without competing for the same responsibilities. For Beryl, the strength of their partnership lies partly in recognising that they bring different qualities to the business. “Bright doesn’t need any motivation. He’s motivated by himself,” she said. “But I think our dynamic, we’ve come to understand each other in terms of what I do versus what he does. Even in the business, we don’t do the same thing. If it’s a Bright thing, it’s Bright. If it’s my thing, it’s me. So we sort of have a dynamic that makes it work that way.” That division of responsibilities has helped them work together while maintaining distinct roles. Rather than trying to lead in the same areas, they have learnt to recognise where each person can contribute most effectively. Beryl serves as Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Echo House Ghana Limited. Her career has earned her recognition in Ghana’s business community, including a place among the country’s Top 50 Young CEOs in 2019 and the Female Young Achiever’s Award at the 2020 EMY Africa Awards. She has also been associated with the creation of Tidal Rave, a major youth-oriented beach festival that has become a prominent fixture on Ghana’s entertainment calendar. Her experience reflects a wider theme in EchoHouse’s development: starting with an idea, learning through experience and continuing to build. The Master of Business Creation programme gave the couple an opportunity to deepen their entrepreneurial knowledge and strengthen their approach to the business they have spent years developing. Their experience illustrates the demands of building a company without a formal academic background in its industry. It also highlights the need for entrepreneurs to keep acquiring skills as their businesses grow and their responsibilities change. For Beryl and Bright, the academic experience came with the added challenge of studying alongside a spouse who is also a business partner. Their success required them to manage assignments and meetings while keeping the company running. The graduation, therefore, was not simply the end of a year of study. It marked another stage in a longer process of learning and adaptation that began when they were students building a university magazine. Their journey has not been one of having every answer from the beginning. Instead, it has involved making decisions, learning new skills and pushing through difficult periods while keeping a shared ambition in view. The joint valedictorian honour brings that journey into focus. The couple who began building EchoHouse as university students have continued to invest in their own development while managing the demands of marriage, parenthood and entrepreneurship. They now hope to apply the lessons from the classroom to take the business to its next level. For Beryl and Bright, the achievement is more than an academic distinction. It reflects a partnership in which both have had to grow, adapt and make room for each other’s strengths. From a university magazine to a company operating across eight countries, their story traces the evolution of an idea into an international business—and of two young entrepreneurs who have continued learning together along the way. At graduation, they stood side by side not only as business partners, but as husband and wife, sharing the recognition that followed years of building together.

items.title: Rivers ADC inaugurates 600-man campaign council
items.description: …alleges abandonment of governance in Rivers By Davies Iheamnachor Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has inaugurated its Governorship Campaign Council. The council composed of 600 persons is chaired by the Sen. (Ohna) Andrew Uchendu was inaugurated with Hon. Chimbiko Akarolo as the Director General. Addressing members of the council during the inauguration in Port Harcourt, Monday, the State Chairman of the Party, Chief (Dr) Chukwudi Dimkpa, charged members of the council to discharge their duties with utmost sense of responsibility. He said: “Having duly presented the leadership, directorates, departments, and membership of the River States 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, and acting in my capacity as the state chairman of the ADC River States, I hereby formally inaugurate the campaign council. “I charge every member to discharge his or her responsibilities faithfully, diligently, and in accordance with the constitution of our party, the approved terms of reference, and the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” Dimkpa, who officially handed the responsibility of the governorship campaign of the party in the state to the team, enjoined the council to work in unity and be result driven. He said: “I now formally hand over the responsibility for the coordination and execution of our governorship campaign to the campaign council under the leadership of distinguished Senator Andrew Uchendu as chairman and Honorable Chimbiko Akarolo as Director-General, subject to the overall authority and policy direction of the state party leadership.” “I expect this council to operate as one united, disciplined, and result-oriented team. By this declaration, the River States ADC 2027 Campaign Council is hereby formally inaugurated.” In his acceptance speech, the Chairman of the Campaign Council, Sen. Andrew Uchendu, regretted that some political elites in the state had converted the state to a battle field, noting that the party would rescue the state from such grip. Uchendu alleged that governance in the state has been abandoned, stressing that the administration of Sir Siminalayi Fubara has failed the state. He said ADC was interested in stabilising leadership in the state, adding that the party wants a situation where the Executive, Legislature and the Judiciary would carry out their responsibilities independently. Uchendu noted that the state was not created for one man to own or control, regretting that recent political crisis had wrecked damage on the state. He said: “While Godfathers wage private wars of ego in Abuja and Port Harcourt, governance in Rivers State has been completely abandoned. An elected government has been decapitated by legislative rascality. Healthcare has collapsed. “Hospital bills by previous administrations have been left to rot, leaving ordinary mothers and infants without access to basic medicine. Schools are abandoned. Our children sit on the floor. “While neighbouring states build for the future, our state is paralyzed by executive/legislative drama and Godfatherism. Our state is rich, but our people are poor. We produce oil that feeds the nation, but we have no light, no good roads, no clean water. “This administration has failed, and will continue to fail. For four years going, we lost the state, the sovereignty of the state. And we have been told that we will lose another four years. God forbid.” Uchendu said the task ahead is that the party must rescue the state from the grip of Godfatherism, urging members of the council to take the rescue message of ADC to the units and ward and local government areas of the state. He also declared that the party would be focused on non-violent and issue based campaign, adding that every vote in the forthcoming election must count. He said: “That is why ADC is here. We want a state where the legislature will do their work, the executive will do their work, the judiciary will do their work. On behalf of the people, not on behalf of themselves. “Our task is clear. We must rescue what we have before, that has been lost. We must recover and rebuild our state for ourselves and our children yet more. And take it to where we believe it should be. Our task is very clear. Take our rescue message to all the 23 local government areas of River State. “Run an issue-based campaign. Non-violent campaign. Unite all tribes. We are one people. We will need to unite our people and fight as a common front. And therefore, run a government that is fair, inclusive.” The post Rivers ADC inaugurates 600-man campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Titre de séjour « Métiers en tension » : attention, urgence absolue
items.description: C’est une alerte pressante adressée à tous les travailleurs sans papiers installés en France : la période transitoire de régularisation liée au dispositif des « métiers en tension » arrive à son terme le 31 décembre. Passé cette date, un vide juridique menaçant pourrait complexifier durablement vos démarches pour l’obtention d’un titre de séjour . Voici pourquoi il est impératif d'agir dès maintenant. Si vous exercez actuellement une activité professionnelle sans titre de séjour dans des secteurs en pénurie de main-d'œuvre — tels que le bâtiment (BTP), la restauration, le nettoyage, la logistique ou l’aide à la personne —, chaque semaine compte. Le dispositif exceptionnel issu de la loi du 26 janvier 2024 (article L. 421-42 du CESEDA) permettait jusqu'alors de solliciter une admission exceptionnelle au séjour de manière autonome, en s'affranchissant du pouvoir discrétionnaire de l’employeur. C’est le constat d'alerte que je dresse en tant que avocat au barreau de Paris : l’articulation entre ce dispositif législatif et l'évolution des instructions ministérielles, notamment la circulaire de février 2025, expose les demandeurs à une insécurité juridique majeure à compter du 1 ᵉʳ janvier 2027 en l'absence de prolongation explicite. Un droit d'accès autonome fragilisé Ce titre de séjour temporaire a constitué une avancée substantielle pour de nombreux travailleurs : L'indépendance vis-à-vis de l’employeur : le dépôt du dossier en préfecture ne requiert pas le formulaire CERFA signé par l'entreprise, mettant fin au levier de dépendance ou au chantage à l’embauche. La reconnaissance de l'intégration professionnelle : la procédure repose sur la démonstration de l'ancienneté de la présence en France et l'exercice effectif d'un métier en tension à travers les bulletins de paie. Des milliers de travailleurs, qui vivent, travaillent et cotisent sur le territoire national en répondant à des besoins structurels de l'économie, se trouvent aujourd'hui dans l'incertitude quant à la pérennité de cette voie de régularisation. Pourquoi faut-il saisir la préfecture sans attendre ? À l'approche du 31 décembre, l'incertitude quant au maintien ou à la modification des critères d'éligibilité fait peser un risque de blocage administratif. Si vous remplissez les conditions requises — ancienneté de résidence, insertion professionnelle avérée dans un secteur concerné et maîtrise minimale de la langue française —, il est vivement conseillé de ne pas différer le dépôt de votre dossier. Anticiper dès à présent permet de sécuriser l'enregistrement de votre demande auprès des services préfectoraux et de vous faire accompagner par un professionnel du droit pour constituer un dossier rigoureux. *Avocat au Barreau de Paris L’article Titre de séjour « Métiers en tension » : attention, urgence absolue est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Nana Yaa Jantuah calls for sanctions over leaked GTA memo involving Maame Efua Houadjeto and Abeiku Santana
items.description: Presidential Staffer Nana Yaa Jantuah has called for sanctions against the person who leaked an internal memo involving Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) Chief Executive Officer Maame Efua Houadjeto and her deputy, Abeiku Santana, insisting that confidential official correspondence must not be released without authorisation. She said the disclosure raised serious concerns about the handling of official information within the public service and urged the relevant authorities to establish how the document found its way into the public domain. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Monday, October 26, Nana Jantuah questioned the motive behind the leak, saying that internal disagreements should be addressed through the appropriate channels rather than exposed publicly. “This is an internal memo. And once it’s an internal communication, whoever brought it out has to be sanctioned,” she said. “I do not think that it’s something that should even have come out like that. So I ask myself who brought out the letter in the public domain. What does the person seek to achieve?” She said the public disclosure of such correspondence could undermine the standards expected of public officials, particularly when the information had not been authorised for release. Referring to the code of ethics governing the public service, she said that staff had a responsibility to protect internal communications. “Because within the code of ethics of the public service, information that is internal, if not authorised, should not be put out,” she stated. The presidential staffer also questioned how the document could have been obtained by the media, suggesting that someone with access to the correspondence may have shared it without permission. When asked whether a journalist could have intercepted the memo, Ms Jantuah challenged the suggestion and called for scrutiny of the procedures for handling official documents. “How do you intercept it? Then it means that the assistants are loose,” she said. She said that the document was unlikely to have reached the public without the involvement of someone familiar with the internal workings of the institutions concerned. “Within the public service, if you are working in there, somebody should have given it to you. You can’t just intercept it. How did you intercept it? Did you catch it in the sky or something?” she asked. She said the possibility that someone within the relevant offices had disclosed the correspondence was troubling and warranted attention. “Somebody within the relevant secretariat could have given it to you. Between the ministry and the GTA. And that is troublesome,” she added. This follows a letter from the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) in charge of Marketing and Special Duties, Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey aka Santana , sent to the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, raising concerns about difficulties accessing GTA Chief Executive Officer Maame Efua Houadjeto for official consultations. Mrs Houadjeto responded by defending her approach to staff engagement and proposing measures to improve communication and coordination between their offices.

items.title: Krobo Girls’ Presbyterian SHS launches centenary cloth to celebrate 100 years of excellence
items.description: Krobo Girls’ Presbyterian Senior High School has launched its Centenary Cloth and a new Krobo Old Girls Association (KOGA) cloth as part of activities to celebrate the school’s century-long legacy of academic excellence and women’s empowerment. The launch, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the Cecilia Obenewah Appiah Hall, brought together school authorities, clergy, students, old students and other guests to commemorate the institution’s contribution to quality education. Held under the theme, “Celebrating a Century of Excellence: A Legacy of Empowering Young Women Through Quality Education,” the event highlighted the school’s commitment to nurturing generations of young women through education. The ceremony was chaired by Mercy Naa Kwaakor Ampah-Bennin, while the school’s Headmistress, Bernice Noel Mensah-Akutteh, hosted the event. Patience Asafo-Adjei, Assistant Head of Administration, outlined the purpose of the gathering, while Rev. Gideon Buenor Pulpulampu, Chairperson of the Dangme Tongu Presbytery, delivered a brief message. Speaking at the launch, the KOGA President highlighted the association’s longstanding role in preserving the school’s heritage, noting that KOGA had spearheaded the production of commemorative cloths for the institution’s major milestones over the past 50 years. She noted that Krobo Girls’ Presbyterian SHS had trained thousands of women who were making significant contributions in their chosen professions across the globe. The KOGA President also disclosed that the two cloths were designed by Lady Cynthia Adjoa Kumi, a member of KOGA ’93 and KOGA US, who generously contributed her time and creativity to the project. The programme featured the official unveiling of the centenary cloth and souvenirs, a presentation on the symbolism and significance of the cloth designs, and an auction of the first pieces. Musical performances and messages from KOGA representatives also formed part of the celebration. A prayer was offered for the sustainability of the school, with hopes for its continued growth and development as it builds on its rich educational heritage. As the school prepares to mark its 100th anniversary in March 2027, all old students were encouraged to begin preparations now and actively participate in the upcoming centenary celebrations. The milestone presents an opportunity for past students to reconnect, celebrate their shared heritage, honour the institution’s rich history and contribute to its continued growth and development. Musical performances and messages from KOGA representatives also formed part of the celebration. A prayer was offered for the sustainability of the school, with hopes for its continued growth and development as it builds on its rich educational heritage. As the school prepares to mark its 100th anniversary in March 2027, all old students were encouraged to begin preparations now and actively participate in the upcoming centenary celebrations. The milestone presents an opportunity for past students to reconnect, celebrate their shared heritage, honour the institution’s rich history and contribute to its continued growth and development.

items.title: Changement au Cameroun : Abdouraman Hamadou Babba présente 10 retombées en cas de victoire de l’opposition aux élections de 2027
items.description: © JDC Le dirigeant sportif et nouvel homme politique mobilise l’électorat en faveur d’une élection massive des candidats que l’opposition investira aux élections législatives et municipales prévues en 2027. Contrôle de l’Assemblée nationale, du Sénat, du gouvernement, libération des prisonniers politiques sont entre autres avantages que le peuple du changement peut gagner en cas de victoire de l’opposition aux prochaines élections. Dans une publication aux allures de message de campagne électorale, Abdouraman Hamadou Babba amène les électeurs à voir au-delà de la participation au scrutin. Le choix qui en résulte ainsi que le résultat global peuvent marquer le départ d’un nouveau Cameroun. 10 retombées se cachent ainsi derrière une victoire de l’opposition à ces deux élections qui s’annoncent. L’acquisition d’une majorité à l’Assemblée nationale et dans la plupart des conseils municipaux mettra l’Assemblée nationale sous le contrôle des acteurs du changement. Le Premier ministre et la majorité des membres du gouvernement proviendront de l’opposition. Les problèmes des populations seront au centre du budget de l’Etat. Les prisonniers politiques seront libres. A cela s’ajoutent l’adoption d’un nouveau code électoral. La mise sur pied d’un organe indépendant chargé de l’organisation et de la supervision des élections. La mise sur pied d’une commission d’enquête parlementaire chargée de faire la lumière sur le processus électoral de 2025. Le contrôle du Sénat dès mars 2028. Une révision de la Constitution supprimera le poste de vice-président et nomination de six des 11 membres du Conseil constitutionnel par l’opposition sera possible. Cependant, si ces résultats sont comme des objectifs à atteindre pour les acteurs du changement, ces derniers ont beaucoup d’efforts à fournir pour les atteindre. La mobilisation des électeurs constitue une partie de ces efforts. Certains acteurs du changement n’assurent pas une implantation sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Ils ne peuvent mobiliser que là où c’est possible. Ils sont en compétition avec d’autres acteurs tenant le pouvoir ainsi que ceux qui leur sont proches. Sur le terrain ils vont se partager les électeurs. Aussi, les acteurs du changement n’appartiennent pas à un même et unique parti politique. Il revient à ces derniers de se rapprocher les uns des autres par différents mécanismes pour conjuguer leurs efforts. Il est plus facile pour eux d’aller en rangs dispersés que de coaliser pour faire bloc en face de l’actuel camp qui est majoritaire tant dans les communes, à l’Assemblée, au Sénat et au sein du gouvernement. Cet article Changement au Cameroun : Abdouraman Hamadou Babba présente 10 retombées en cas de victoire de l’opposition aux élections de 2027 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: South Africa evacuee alleges NPP members coached returnees to criticise government payments
items.description: A representative of Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa following xenophobic attacks, Michael Addo, has alleged that some returnees were contacted and coached by members of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) to criticise the government’s financial support package. Speaking to the media on Monday, October 26, Mr Addo said the evacuees were determined to share their experiences truthfully, regardless of their political affiliations. He insisted that partisan interests would not influence their accounts of the assistance received from the government. “We are aware that some members of our group have received calls and coaching to speak against the government, but our conscience will not allow us to do so, even if we support the opposition party rather than the government of the day,” he said. Mr Addo also disputed claims that some returnees received only GH¢500 as transportation support, while others were paid only the GH¢5,000 reintegration allowance. According to him, all members of the group received the full GH¢5,500 package, comprising GH¢5,000 for reintegration and GH¢500 for transportation, on their respective arrival dates. He urged the public to focus on the facts rather than allow political considerations to shape the discussion surrounding the evacuation exercise. “It is only fair that we state the facts and refuse to allow petty politics to make us liars,” he said, rejecting claims of shortfalls in the payments. Background The comments come amid growing public scrutiny of the government’s expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa following xenophobic attacks. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has also defended the payment arrangements, dismissing allegations that some returnees received less than the announced GH¢5,500 package. He has maintained that all 1,000 Ghanaians on the evacuation list, including minors, received the full amount. The minister has also said the ministry has not received complaints about alleged payment shortfalls. The competing claims have intensified the debate over the payments, with questions being raised about the accuracy of the records and the accountability of funds used for the exercise.

items.title: Le « Maître de la Parole » s’est éteint : Mon vibrant hommage à Séné Diallo, un frère et un monument des médias
items.description: C’est avec une douleur indicible que j’ai découvert, dès mon réveil ce matin, ce titre déchirant de Mosaiqueguinee : « Médias : l’animateur Séné Diallo s’est éteint cette nuit ! » Celui qui m’appelait si affectueusement « Bappa » vient de refermer les yeux pour toujours, me plongeant, ainsi que l’ensemble du monde des médias guinéens, dans une profonde tristesse. Mon histoire avec Séné a commencé en 2008. Je venais alors de lancer la toute première émission de ma radio privée, Horizon FM : « Libre antenne », un espace interactif et novateur diffusé en quatre langues. Un jour, Séné a poussé la porte de la station. Il s’est présenté à moi en sa qualité de chargé de communication et des relations publiques de Cellcom Guinée . Il ne venait pas les mains vides : il apportait une excellente nouvelle, concrétisée par une offre de collaboration et un grand contrat de partenariat. Cette promesse, il l’a tenue avec la promptitude et le professionnalisme qui le caractérisaient. Depuis ce jour fondateur, Séné est resté un ami d'une loyauté rare, un homme de confiance qui veillait sur la radio, même à distance. Il est parti bien trop tôt. Malgré ce vide immense, il laisse derrière lui des milliers de disciples. Ils reçoivent aujourd'hui en héritage sa voix d'or, son souci permanent de la perfection et son amitié indéfectible. Je salue la mémoire d’un véritable maître de la parole, un homme de cœur que la poussière de l’oubli ne couvrira jamais. Adieu, mon cher Séné. Repose en paix. C’est toute la Guinée reconnaissante qui te pleure aujourd'hui et qui prie pour que ton âme repose éternellement dans les jardins fleuris du paradis. Boubacar Yacine Diallo Journaliste-Écrivain , Président de la haute autorité de la communication

items.title: Brésil : Après le père Jair Bolsonaro, Lula da Silva bat le fils Flávio Bolsonaro à l’élection présidentielle
items.description: Le président de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a remporté l'élection présidentielle brésilienne du dimanche 25 octobre 2026, avec 51,79 % des voix, contre 48,21 % pour le candidat d'extrême droite Flávio Bolsonaro. Arrivé en deuxième position au premier tour, il a renversé la tendance face au fils de l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro (2019-2022). Avec près de 51,8 % des voix contre 48,2 % pour Flávio Bolsonaro, le président sortant, âgé de 80 ans, a déjoué les pronostics. C'est une première dans l'histoire électorale du Brésil. Depuis le retour à la démocratie, aucun candidat arrivé en deuxième position au premier tour n'avait réussi à remporter le second. « Les Brésiliens sont allés voter parce que nous avons réussi à les convaincre que le vote était très important pour garantir la démocratie », a déclaré Lula da Silva depuis São Paulo. L'ancien syndicaliste a obtenu environ 4,4 millions de voix de plus que son adversaire, alors qu'il avait été devancé par ce dernier au premier tour, le 4 octobre. À l'annonce des résultats, Flávio Bolsonaro a refusé de reconnaître sa défaite et annoncé son intention de demander l'annulation du scrutin, contestant notamment la décision de prolonger les heures de vote. Son père, Jair Bolsonaro, avait lui aussi refusé de reconnaître sa défaite face à Lula en 2022. Il purge actuellement une peine de 27 ans de prison pour son implication dans une tentative de coup d'État après sa défaite électorale. Pour ce quatrième mandat le chef de l'État brésilien, Lula da Silva, devra toutefois composer avec un Parlement marqué par une forte présence conservatrice, ce qui pourrait limiter sa marge de manœuvre. Précisons que Lula da Silva, l'un des dirigeants les plus âgés à exercer la fonction présidentielle, aura 85 ans à la fin de son mandat, en 2030. Il totalisera alors quatre mandats présidentiels. items.title: LHC disposes of petition seeking release of Imran's sisters after govt extends detention
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday disposed of a petition seeking the release of PTI founder Imran Khan’s three sisters after the Punjab government informed the court that their preventive detention had been extended for another 30 days. An assistant advocate general of Punjab told Justice Abher Gul Khan, who has been holding hearings on the petition, that the government had approved a further 30-day detention of Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi on the recommendation of the Lahore deputy commissioner. The law officer also submitted a report on behalf of the home secretary and said the detention period had been extended on Oct 7. Imran’s sisters — Aleema, Noreen and Uzma — were detained by authorities in September, under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI geared up for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Their detention was ordered for 30 days and expired on Oct 19 for Aleema and Oct 20 for Uzma and Noreen, the petitioner’s counsel had said at the previous hearing. Today, counsel Rana Mudassar Umar requested the court to order the recovery of the three women and their production before the court. However, Justice Khan observed that while the deputy commissioner had issued the detention notifications, but the petitioner had not made the official a respondent in the petition. The judge held that the court could not issue an order beyond the scope of the petition. The judge disposed of the petition in light of the home secretary’s report. Aleema’s son, Shahrez, had filed the petition alleging that the three sisters remained confined at Kot Lakhpat jail despite the end of their initial 30-day detention orders on Oct 19 for Aleema and 20 for Noreen and Uzma. The petition stated that the women were taken into custody in September under Section 3 of the MPO, 1960. Aleema was detained on Sept 20, while Uzma and Noreen were detained a day later. The petitioner argued that the continuous detention beyond the notified period was unlawful, that the sisters were not wanted in any criminal case and that preventive detention could not be used as a substitute for ordinary criminal law. It asked the court to order the sisters’ immediate release and that they be produced before the court.

items.title: TOR revival boosts Burkina Faso fuel supply through Ghana to 40% – Kombat
items.description: The share of Burkina Faso’s petroleum product movements through Ghana has increased from 15 per cent in 2024 to 40 per cent, as the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) and other petroleum sector institutions strengthen Ghana’s role as a regional fuel supply hub. Managing Director of TOR, Edmond Kombat, said the increase reflected improved collaboration among petroleum sector institutions and renewed confidence in Ghana’s capacity to support regional petroleum supply arrangements. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, he said the refinery’s recovery was contributing to fuel security in Ghana and neighbouring Sahelian countries. Mr Kombat said the refinery’s relationship with the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited (BOST) and other petroleum service providers had helped facilitate the movement of petroleum products through Ghana. “TOR’s close working relationship with NPA, BOST and other Petroleum Service providers has ensured Burkina Faso’s National Oil Company has increased its petroleum products movement through Ghana from 15% in 2024 to 40% as at today,” he said. The Managing Director said restoring TOR’s operations was important not only for Ghana’s domestic energy security but also for strengthening the country’s position in the regional petroleum supply chain. He explained that the refinery had previously been reduced largely to storage activities after its major processing units were shut down. The CDU had been out of operation since April 2021, while the Residue Fluid Catalytic Cracking unit had been shut down since 2019. Following the current management’s appointment in May 2025, a turnaround maintenance programme was undertaken to rehabilitate the CDU, paving the way for refining operations to resume on December 19, 2025. Mr Kombat said the refinery had since received several crude cargoes, including Ghanaian indigenous crude, and had recorded substantial growth in product storage volumes. Storage volumes increased from 426,954 metric tonnes in 2024 to 1,107,389 metric tonnes in 2025, before rising further to 1,350,000 metric tonnes in 2026, according to figures presented by management. He said TOR’s recovery, combined with cooperation among state institutions and petroleum service providers, had improved its capacity to support petroleum supply arrangements. The Managing Director also argued that domestic refining capacity could help reduce Ghana’s exposure to disruptions in international fuel supplies and support greater price stability. He said the refinery’s partnership with GOIL, including an engagement on September 2, 2026, was intended to increase the supply of locally refined products. Mr Kombat added that the government’s longer-term plan to expand TOR’s processing capacity to 100,000 barrels per day, with a further ambition of 200,000 barrels per day, would strengthen Ghana’s refining capabilities. He said management would continue working with industry partners to consolidate the refinery’s recovery and improve its contribution to Ghana’s energy security and regional petroleum trade.

Le FSB annonce avoir déjoué une attaque de drones contre la défense antimissile de Moscou
items.description: Le Service federal de securite russe (FSB) a annonce, le 26 octobre, avoir empeche un projet d'attaque de drones contre un element cle du systeme de defense antimissile de Moscou et une infrastructure electrique. Deux hommes originaires du Caucase du Sud, nes en 1991 et 1998, ont ete arretes. Selon le FSB, les suspects agissaient sur instruction du Service de securite d'Ukraine (SBU). D'apres les autorites russes, l'un des deux hommes aurait ete recrute par un agent du SBU, qui lui aurait promis une remuneration pour mener l'operation. Il se serait ensuite rendu en Russie et aurait sollicite une connaissance pour participer a sa preparation. Les suspects auraient recupere des drones FPV et des composants d'engins explosifs artisanaux dans des caches situees dans les regions de Smolensk et de Kalouga. Leur mission consistait a preparer les appareils, a les acheminer vers un point de lancement dans la region de Moscou, puis a les activer avant leur decollage. Le pilotage devait etre assure a distance depuis le territoire ukrainien. Un tel appareil permet a son operateur de le diriger grâce aux images transmises en direct par une camera embarquee. Les services russes affirment avoir empeche l'attaque avant son execution Le FSB affirme avoir decouvert les preparatifs en amont et place les suspects sous surveillance. Il indique aussi avoir identifie le representant ukrainien presume charge de superviser l'operation. Selon les informations communiquees par les autorites russes, les drones auraient deja ete configures et achemines vers leur point de lancement. Les deux hommes ont ete interpelles avant le decollage des appareils, ce qui aurait empeche l'attaque contre les installations visees. Un agent du FSB a souligne que l'operation visait a eviter des victimes parmi la population civile et a prevenir des dommages aux infrastructures. Les services russes ont precise avoir poursuivi, apres les arrestations, un « jeu operationnel » avec les contacts ukrainiens des suspects dans le cadre du contre-espionnage. Des poursuites judiciaires et un avertissement des services russes Selon le FSB, une procedure penale a ete ouverte contre les deux hommes pour participation a une communaute terroriste, au titre de la deuxieme partie de l'article 205.4 du Code penal russe. Un tribunal a ordonne leur placement en detention provisoire. Les suspects encourent jusqu'a 15 ans de prison. L'enquete se poursuit afin d'etablir les circonstances de l'affaire, de determiner les responsabilites et d'identifier d'eventuels complices. Dans son communique du 26 octobre, le FSB a reaffirme que les services ukrainiens cherchaient a recruter des civils pour mener des operations de sabotage sur le territoire russe . Il a aussi averti que les personnes apportant leur soutien a ces activites seraient identifiees et poursuivies conformement a la legislation russe.

items.title: Week-End des Lions : les Sénégalais font vibrer l’Europe
items.description: Nicolas Jackson en feu, Tidiam Gomis buteur avec Leipzig, Yehvann Diouf décisif avec Nice et Sadibou Sané solide face à Lille : les Lions ont animé les pelouses européennes ce week-end. Tour d’horizon des performances des Sénégalais sur les pelouses européennes. Jackson et Mbaye corrigent Iliman Ndiaye Le choc entre Aston Villa et Manchester City a tourné à l’avantage des Villans, portés par un Nicolas Jackson particulièrement inspiré. Samedi, l’attaquant sénégalais a inscrit les deux buts de son équipe lors d’une victoire 2-1 qui met fin à l’invincibilité des Citizens en championnat cette saison. Jackson a lancé les siens dès la 6e minute, avant de reprendre l’avantage pour Aston Villa à l’heure de jeu. À la 60e minute, il a conclu une action initiée par Ibrahim Mbaye, entré en jeu une minute plus tôt. Ce deuxième but a permis aux hommes d’Aston Villa de prendre définitivement les devants. En face, Iliman Ndiaye s’est également illustré. L’attaquant sénégalais de Manchester City a délivré la passe décisive sur l’égalisation d’Erling Haaland à la 52e minute. Mais cette contribution n’a pas suffi à éviter la défaite aux Citizens. Cette rencontre aura ainsi mis en lumière trois internationaux sénégalais, chacun ayant contribué à l’un des buts inscrits. Pour Jackson, ce doublé constitue une nouvelle performance marquante depuis son arrivée à Aston Villa. Il porte à quatre son total de buts en Premier League et à sept celui de ses réalisations toutes compétitions confondues. Sadibou Sané solide, Lamine Camara fautif sur le but des Gones L’AS Monaco et Lille se sont neutralisés (1-1), dimanche, lors de la 8e journée de Ligue 1. Titulaire dans l’axe de la défense monégasque, Sadibou Sané a livré une prestation solide, avec 11 ballons récupérés, selon les statistiques relevées. Le défenseur sénégalais s’est montré actif dans les interventions et les premières relances, contribuant à la résistance de son équipe face aux offensives lilloises. Son compatriote Lamine Camara a, en revanche, connu un moment difficile. Le milieu de terrain monégasque a perdu le ballon dans son propre camp sous le pressing de Ngal’ayel Mukau, une erreur exploitée par Lille pour ouvrir le score. Après une passe en profondeur de Soriba Diaoune, Ethan Mbappé a conclu l’action à la 24e minute. Malgré cette perte de balle coûteuse, Camara a continué à s’investir dans les duels et la récupération. Monaco a finalement arraché le nul grâce à Edan Diop à la 74e minute. Yehvann Diouf sauve Nice après sa bourde En Ligue 1 française, Yehvann Diouf a vécu une soirée riche en émotions avec l’OGC Nice. En déplacement à Brest, vendredi, le gardien sénégalais et ses coéquipiers se sont imposés 2-1 après avoir été menés au score. Surpris par Ludovic Ajorque dès la 15e minute, le portier niçois a dû attendre la fin de la rencontre pour connaître son moment décisif. Alors que Brest avait l’occasion de revenir au score sur penalty dans le temps additionnel, Diouf a repoussé la tentative de Kenny Lala à la 90e+10 minute. Un arrêt déterminant qui a permis aux Aiglons de conserver leur avantage et de repartir avec les trois points. Le gardien sénégalais confirme ainsi sa capacité à répondre présent dans les moments de forte pression. Pape Moussa Fall inscrit son huitième but avec Metz En Ligue 2 française, Pape Moussa Fall a également trouvé le chemin des filets. L’attaquant du FC Metz a ouvert le score dès la 9e minute face à Dunkerque, vendredi. Malgré cette entame favorable, les Messins n’ont pas réussi à conserver leur avantage. Opa Sangante a égalisé pour Dunkerque à la 65e minute, scellant le score à 1-1. Pour Fall, cette réalisation constitue néanmoins un motif de satisfaction dans une rencontre où son équipe a laissé échapper la victoire. Le Sénégalais a rapidement permis à Metz de prendre les devants, sans que cela suffise à faire la différence au classement. Mamour Ndiaye enchaîne les clean sheets À Saint-Étienne, Mamour Ndiaye poursuit son apprentissage dans les buts. Le jeune gardien sénégalais a disputé une nouvelle rencontre comme titulaire avec les Verts, samedi, lors de la réception de Nantes en Ligue 2. Saint-Étienne s’est imposé 1-0, permettant au portier de conserver sa cage inviolée. Cette nouvelle prestation s’inscrit dans la continuité de sa première titularisation, conclue par une victoire sur le même score face au Red Star, le 17 octobre. À 20 ans, Mamour Ndiaye profite ainsi du temps de jeu qui lui est accordé pour engranger de l’expérience et défendre ses chances dans la hiérarchie stéphanoise. Sadio Mané décisif avec Al-Nassr En Arabie saoudite, Sadio Mané était également en action avec Al-Nassr vendredi. L’attaquant sénégalais a disputé 86 minutes lors de la rencontre de son équipe contre Al-Faysaly. Sa participation confirme qu’il reste impliqué dans la campagne de son club, même si les informations consultées ne permettent pas de lui attribuer une action décisive sur cette rencontre. Entre le doublé de Jackson, les passes décisives de Mbaye et Ndiaye, l’arrêt décisif de Diouf et les buts de Fall, les Sénégalais ont animé plusieurs championnats européens au cours du week-end. Des performances individuelles variées, avec des contributions aussi bien offensives que défensives. Tidiam Gomis de nouveau buteur en championnat Tidiam Gomis poursuit sur sa lancée avec le RB Leipzig. Après avoir marqué contre le Real Madrid en Ligue des champions, mercredi, l’attaquant de 20 ans a récidivé samedi en Bundesliga face à Elversberg. Il a ouvert le score à la 48e minute lors de la victoire des siens (4-0), confirmant sa bonne dynamique offensive. Né en France et international dans les catégories de jeunes françaises, Tidiam Gomis possède également des attaches sénégalaises qui en font un profil à suivre pour les Lions. Son parcours en sélection de jeunes ne ferme pas, à lui seul, la porte à un éventuel changement de nationalité sportive. Lors de la Coupe du monde U17 de 2023 qu’il a disputée avec la France, le jeune attaquant aurait manifesté son souhait de représenter un jour le Sénégal. Yaya SOW

items.title: A Halloween Myth That Can Finally Die
items.description: Toddler parenting is an exercise in picking battles, and one I almost never pick is the battle over sugar. Quite often, my 2-and-a-half-year-old eats just a few bites of his meal before proclaiming himself “done, done, done,” yet mysteriously also desirous of dessert. Generally, at this point, I’ll give him a cookie, or whatever sweet he’s fixated on—yes, even if he hasn’t finished his healthy dinner, or if it’s almost bedtime, or if we’re somewhere I need him to behave. I feel good about these choices because: science. For one thing, the American Academy of Pediatrics’ recommendations on added sugar are generous, allowing for more than an entire Klondike bar’s worth of it a day. For another, sugar doesn’t make kids hyper. The sooner parents internalize this, the sooner they can drop sugar policing from the dreaded mental load and reapportion that slot to some other parental drudgery, such as keeping track of spirit days . Wherever a child is tipping over a bin of Legos or jumping on a couch, a “sugar rush” is bound to be blamed. Popular shows including The Office and Abbott Elementary have episodes in which characters eat too much sugar, go into overdrive, and crash. I’m often warned by other moms not to give my son anything sweet—by which I guess they mean any and all toddler food—before naptime. Their admonitions, however, are misguided. “I know parents, and many people would love to be able to point the finger at sugar” when a child acts up, Jill Castle, a pediatric dietitian, told me. “But it just doesn’t hold up in the research.” A series of studies from the 1980s and ’90s, led by a prominent pediatrician named Mark Wolraich, helped break the connection between sugar and hyperactivity, which is generally defined as restlessness, poor behavior, and impulsivity. In 1985, Wolraich and his colleagues studied 16 hyperactive boys who were fed a clinically monitored, sugar-free diet for a day, then given either a sugary or an artificially sweetened drink. The researchers found no difference in behavior or cognition between the boys who consumed the sugary drink and those who had the sugar-free one. In a 1994 double-blind, controlled trial , Wolraich found that when kids ate a high-sugar diet for three weeks, they performed no differently on a series of behavioral and cognitive measures than when they ate little sugar. In a 1995 meta-analy s is , he examined the results of 23 studies and concluded that “sugar does not affect the behavior or cognitive performance of children.” [ Read: How baby-led weaning almost ruined my life ] For some children, sugar can have a slight sedative effect, and regularly consuming way too much can eventually put kids at risk for type 2 diabetes and obesity. The AAP recommends that kids ages 2 to 18 have no more than 25 grams of added sugar a day, the equivalent of about three fun-sized packages of M&Ms. (The guidance doesn’t apply to naturally occurring sugar, including the kind in fruit.) On special occasions such as Halloween, exceeding this limit is fine, Gwen Cook, a pediatrician at the University of Utah Hospital, told me. Many pediatricians discourage trying to eliminate sugar from a child’s diet entirely, Cook said, because doing so is “unnecessarily restrictive, especially socially.” No one wants to be the kid at a birthday party eating carrot sticks instead of cake. Despite these findings, the sugar-hyperactivity myth has survived for decades because sugary foods tend to be served during celebrations that are otherwise chaotic and overstimulating, such as Halloween, Christmas, and birthdays. Some kids become wired at these festivities because the environment is novel and exciting, not because they’re eating chocolate. “They’re playing games; there’s music or decorations up that are different,” Cook said. “All of those things can feed into a child being more hyperactive . ” Parents may also expect kids to become hyper when they have sweets: In one study , mothers who were told that their kids had consumed a large dose of sugar rated their children as significantly more hyperactive than mothers who were told that their kids had received an artificially sweetened placebo—even though all of the kids had actually ingested the placebo. (This expectancy effect was stronger, the study authors said, for “cognitively rigid mothers.”) When kids eat sugar, parents may be more likely to interpret their behavior as wild, and attribute it to the sugar. So the myth lives on. I also think parents persist in believing that sugar makes kids rambunctious for the same reason they believe in so many other dubious child-rearing fallacies. Parents long for an explanation for their kids’ inexplicable behavior and for a sense of control over it. If sugar really explained why kids became manic and naughty, parents could create peace by banning Skittles and soda. But sugar isn’t to blame, which leaves us to accept our kids for the frenzied, irrational beings that they are.

items.title: Aggregate spending on infrastructure across Ghana, 3 others to increase to $96bn in 2050 – PwC Global Infrastructure Outlook
items.description: Africa will experience the fastest annual growth in infrastructure spending of any region over the 25-year forecast period, according to PwC Global Infrastructure Outlook 2026. Aggregate annual spending across Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa is projected to increase from $54 billion in 2024 to $96 billion in 2050, a 77% increase. According to the report, demographic change and urbanisation are driving growth in Africa. The continent is expected to add more than 800 million urban residents by 2050, and the number of megacities will triple. Spending on transport infrastructure, the largest sector, is projected to more than double as trade corridors expands. Agriculture and resource infrastructure will be the region’s second- and third-largest spending sectors over the forecast period. “We expect the next 25 years to be defined by an unprecedented surge in global infrastructure investment. But there’s no guarantee the required levels of spending will materialise. And top-line revenues don’t automatically translate into profitable investments. To unlock value, investors, governments, and corporations will need a strategic, system‑wide approach that overcomes today’s constraints and accelerates delivery”, the report stated. Key imperatives of such an approach, the report said, include embedding long-term strategic planning. “Political and policy uncertainty and regulatory and planning delays hinder the development of infrastructure and reduce its attractiveness as an investment. At the same time, infrastructure assets are inherently long-lived, often spanning multiple economic and political cycles. To maximise their value, robust frameworks that enable decision-making beyond short-term horizons are needed”, the report pointed out. This means establishing stable regulatory environments and clear national or regional strategies that provide certainty for investors and delivery partners. It urged governments to form independent bodies empowered to make infrastructure investment decisions across political parties. “In parallel, planning and regulatory approval processes must be streamlined to accelerate delivery and reduce uncertainty”. Also, the report mentioned moving from silos to integrated systems . It said concentrating investment in power or digital sectors without making corresponding upgrades in other sectors like transport or water risks creating bottlenecks that may ultimately constrain both returns and growth. Conversely, spreading and coordinating investment across the infrastructure ecosystem unlocks multiplier effects—while also enabling the alignment of capital, capability, and policy to deliver integrated systems that boost productivity and long-term value. It therefore advised the consideration of combining data centre campuses with clean power purchase agreements and water reuse. Similarly, the report talked about innovating financing and partnership mechanisms . It argued that because public budgets alone will be insufficient, institutional investors, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, and private credit providers will be central to the next 25 years of infrastructure development. “What’s needed is more effective and efficient collaboration between governments and the private sector. This includes developing new financing structures, risk-sharing mechanisms, and delivery models that leverage the strengths of both sides. One example is capital recycling, wherein governments sell or lease mature infrastructure assets and reinvest the proceeds into new projects—unlocking funding without increasing public debt”. By 2050, the report said the world will be increasingly dependent on electrification, data, automation, and circular resource flows. And infrastructure will no longer be defined solely by isolated physical assets like roads, grids, or plants.

items.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
items.description: Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war. Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday. Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July. Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August. Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume. Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV. “This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X. “The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.” – ‘Serious tensions’ – On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen. The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month. Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said. “Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday. Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”. Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions. “For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just… sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP. “There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added. “And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.” – ‘Don’t test us’ – Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged. Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28. On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power. “We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said. “Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials. The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied. AFP The post Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: TOR clears six-year audit backlog, submits seven financial reports to SIGA
items.description: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has cleared its backlog of audited financial statements covering 2019 to 2024, bringing an end to six consecutive years without completed audited accounts, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has announced. Mr Kombat said the refinery completed the outstanding accounts by April 30, 2026, before finalising its 2025 accounts on May 30, 2026. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, he said the company had submitted seven audited financial reports to the State Interests and Governance Authority (SIGA), restoring its financial reporting obligations to date. The reports were presented at TOR’s 18th Annual General Meeting on June 30, 2026. According to the Managing Director, SIGA commended the refinery for completing the outstanding reports, which brought it up to date for the first time since the 2018 accounts were filed. “The audited accounts for 2019 to 2024 were completed by April 30, 2026, followed by the 2025 accounts on May 30, 2026,” he said. He explained that the exercise was part of management’s broader commitment to improving transparency, strengthening financial accountability and restoring confidence in the operations of the state-owned refinery. The absence of audited accounts had been among the major governance challenges facing TOR when the current management assumed office in May 2025. Mr Kombat said the company had spent several years without fulfilling its financial reporting obligations, making it necessary for management to review the unaudited accounts and establish a clearer picture of its financial position. He also disclosed that TOR had held its first Annual General Meeting in a long time to consider outstanding financial statements covering multiple years, including the period from 2017 to 2025. The exercise was intended to ensure compliance with statutory requirements and improve the availability of reliable financial information for decision-making. Mr Kombat said the financial reporting reforms were being pursued alongside efforts to reduce liabilities, recover receivables and improve the refinery’s commercial performance. He noted that TOR had also recorded a profit before tax of GH¢1.24 billion in 2025, its first return to profitability in a decade, according to SIGA. The Managing Director said the refinery would continue strengthening its financial management systems as it pursued its recovery programme.
